identityReview: Marina Silva, born February 8, 1958 in Rio Branco, Acre. History graduate, not a claimed doctorate. Former Rio Branco city councillor and Acre state deputy; Senate terms 1995–2003 and 2003–2011 with ministerial leave. Environment minister 2003–2008 and January 1, 2023–April 1, 2026. Current federal deputy for São Paulo, REDE, 2023–2027 term, resumed April 1, 2026. Unsuccessful October 4, 2026 Senate candidate, not senator-elect or current environment minister. No new ministry or climate-authority appointment established.
lifeStatusEvidence: Official MMA account confirms participation as federal deputy at a COP31 panel in Antalya on November 12, 2026. Folhapress journalist Jéssica Maes records a completed in-person interview on November 14, published by Jornal de Brasília November 17. Event, publication and update dates remain distinct; prospective Simon Stiell meeting is not counted as completed.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read legislative profiles and mandate tables, contemporary UOL/Agência Estado and Agência Senado accounts, original official Flickr caption and licence, TRE-SP election result, UNEP award profile, MMA completed COP31 event report and Folhapress interview. Read Commons metadata and licence history. No portrait pixels.
corrections: Read Chamber biography: federal term 2023–2027, sworn February 1, 2023, ministerial leave from February 3 and resumed April 1, 2026. History degree and specialization are different qualifications. City council 1989–1991 and state assembly 1991–1995 precede Senate service. External-mandate rows do not fully describe party changes or continuous active Senate service during ministerial leave.

Read current Chamber profile: active REDE–SP federal deputy; civil name Maria Osmarina Marina da Silva Vaz de Lima, birthday February 8, 1958, birthplace Rio Branco, Acre. This current institutional record overrides stale minister biographies. No personal contact details reproduced; no form submitted.

Read Senate identity, education and mandate tables. Senate terms 1995–2003 and 2003–2011 differ from uninterrupted attendance; ministerial leave is retained. Year-level dates are used rather than inventing exact accession days. Specialized study is not converted into a masters degree or PhD.

Read Fernanda Calgaro’s August 20, 2014 UOL report: PSB nomination following Campos’s death, Albuquerque running mate and remaining coalition ratification step. Biography supports rubber-community childhood, literacy education, 1984 history graduation, union work, earlier elections and policy conflicts. Nomination, registration, polling forecasts and election victory are not interchangeable; no presidential victory claimed.

Read Agência Senado’s May 13, 2008 report. Silva submitted a resignation request that afternoon and a Senate return was prospective in the report. Later return is corroborated by official career records; no assertion that all formal procedures or Senate resumption happened May 13. Senators’ praise is opinion, not independent proof of policy success.

Read UOL’s September 22, 2015 account of TSE’s 7–0 registration approval. The 2013 rejection concerned insufficient validated support signatures. Party-building initiative and later legal registration are separated. No claim to have read the full original court judgment or checked every signature.

Read original Palácio do Planalto Flickr caption: January 1, 2023 swearing-in in Brasília, photographer Ricardo Stuckert/PR, uploaded January 13. This documents the event rather than the departmental handover ceremony on January 4. Caption read does not constitute viewing image pixels. Clicked the licence link, which resolves to CC BY 2.0.

Read Agência Estado’s April 1, 2026 dispatch via UOL: formal departure in DOU Extra and Capobianco’s formal appointment. April 1 is distinct from advance March 31 announcements. Candidate office was undecided in that historical report; subsequent Senate candidacy and defeat are established by the electoral court. No claim to have read the complete DOU issue.

Read TRE-SP’s October 4, 2026 report, updated October 5, with all precincts counted. Silva fourth, 7,862,400 votes and 18.12%; Derrite and Prado won the two seats. These are valid candidate-vote shares, not shares of individual electors; there is no Senate runoff. No personal re-count of ballots or certificate-of-election audit.

Read UNEP’s 2007 Champions of the Earth profile and Policy Leadership classification. Its conservation/community-livelihood and cross-government assessment supports award context. Historic praise and then-current deforestation estimates are not presented as current measurements, independent causal proof or an achievement by Silva alone.

Read MMA’s COP31 report published November 13 and updated November 14. Actual panel occurred November 12 and included federal deputy Silva, minister Capobianco and other officials. Roadmap delivery was Capobianco’s, not Silva’s personal act. Zero deforestation by 2030 is a target, not accomplished zero; agency statistics were not independently reconstructed.

Read Jéssica Maes/Folhapress interview via Jornal de Brasília, published November 17, 2026, recounting November 14 in-person interview in Antalya. Reviewed substantive questions on climate-emergency framework, scientific committee, multi-level governance and fossil-fuel transition. A forthcoming Stiell meeting is not proof it occurred. Potential climate-authority role and ministry return remain speculation, not appointment. Loose year-end deputy wording is superseded by Chamber’s 2023–2027 term.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields in seven foreign languages reviewed against Chinese and English. Preserve current federal deputy rather than minister/senator-elect; Rio Branco birthplace and 1984 history degree; local mandates and two Senate terms with leave; 2008 resignation request; 2014 nomination rather than victory; 2013 rejection versus 2015 registration; January 1 ministry oath versus February 1 deputy oath/February 3 leave; April 1 formal departure/resumption; October 4 fourth place, 7862400/18.12% valid candidate votes; November 12 event/14 interview/17 publication; proposed climate institutions rather than completed appointment.
